post_topic: Why direct API verification beats documentation trust in integration work
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title text at top center: "Verify the Wire Before You Build the Bridge"

Layout flows top to bottom, centered on the page.

At the top center: a box labeled "Integration Planning" with a small document/clipboard icon.

Below it, a downward arrow labeled "Step 1: Direct API Verification (curl)" pointing to a central hexagon node labeled "curl" in bold monospace font.

From the curl node, two arrows branch left and right at roughly 45-degree angles downward.

Left branch arrow is labeled "API Key A" pointing to a box labeled "Key: Valid\nTier: Free\nAPI Access: None" with a red amber-highlighted callout badge reading "403 Forbidden — Tier Wall".

Right branch arrow is labeled "API Key B" pointing to a box labeled "Key: Valid\nPermissions: Correct\nEndpoint: Not Live Yet" with an amber-highlighted callout badge reading "404 — Documented, Not Deployed".

Below both boxes, two downward arrows converge into a single box at the bottom center labeled "Root Cause Found — Before Integration Code Written" with a checkmark icon in blue.

Below that box, a smaller muted-text label reads: "20 min verification session vs. hours of misattributed debugging"

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
